brief: GS's Mitch Jeter Mon 28 Sep desk-color note: the S&P 500 closed -77bps at 7,683 (NDX -108bps, R2K -69bps, Dow -67bps) after a midday report that the US would ease Iran sanctions by releasing frozen assets for nuclear concessions was quickly rebutted by Iranian officials. Oil and rates rose on the back-and-forth, pushing 10Y yields above 5.2% and driving the risk-off tape, with the one-month move in real rates now one of the worst since 2013; GS says equities are through its "negative forward returns" technical levels. Breadth weakened further: the median SPX stock trades 16% below its 52-week high, the worst breadth since the Dot-Com Bubble, with 334 SPX names red on the day. AI/tech underperformed on an OpenAI training pause and Musk's privacy concerns about Meta's Muse agent, plus MDB (-18.5%) after its CEO's move to Meta, partly offset by NVDA's $150bn buyback increase and new AI-safety software platform. The desk was a net seller, with asset managers and hedge funds both better for sale; GS's model projects CTAs selling $5.3bn of RTY futures next week, one of the largest such estimates in 6 years, while dealers stay long S&P gamma but flip short NDX above +4%.
